No fixed version is published, so no dependency range resolves around it: the only path in this repository is the dev-only release toolchain semantic-release -> @semantic-release/commit-analyzer -> micromatch -> braces. The advisory is a denial of service on brace expansion of attacker-supplied patterns; this project never expands untrusted glob input and devDependencies are not part of the published npm archive. Review before 2026-11-20: if braces ships a fix, or micromatch/semantic-release stops depending on it, delete this record; if the exception is still needed, re-justify it and move the date. Any other advisory fails the gate.

GHSA-rxp7-6hxx-x8q5.notes: ip-address <=10.7.3 quadratic-time Address6 zone-identifier match, a denial of service when parsing one very long attacker-supplied string (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rxp7-6hxx-x8q5). Fixed upstream in ip-address@10.7.4, published 2026-10-11, but the only path in this repository is the dev-only release toolchain semantic-release -> @semantic-release/npm@13.2.0 -> npm@^11.6.2 (11.21.1) -> its bundled node_modules/npm/node_modules/ip-address@10.7.2. npm still bundles 10.7.2 in every release that satisfies that range, including 12.2.1, and a bundled dependency cannot be replaced by npm overrides, so no dependency range or lockfile change resolves it today. The project never parses untrusted IPv6 addresses and devDependencies are not part of the published npm archive. Review before 2026-11-20: when an npm release that @semantic-release/npm accepts bundles ip-address >=10.7.4, run npm update npm and delete this record; if the exception is still needed, re-justify it and move the date. Any other advisory fails the gate.
